member.name: M:Graphs.Primitives.CsrGraph.InducedSubgraph(System.Boolean[],System.Int32[]@,System.Int32[]@)
member.summary: Build a new on the subset of nodes selected by . Only edges whose both endpoints are masked are retained; edge weights are copied verbatim. Output node indices are densely renumbered in [0, subN); use to translate back, or for the reverse direction (-1 for nodes that were filtered out).
member.remarks: O(N + E) time and space. The MAPPER-SPC patch driver consumes this: given a Mapper cover bin's preimage, restrict the full proximity graph to that bin's nodes and hand the result to the adaptive SPC scheduler. Output preserves the input's CSR symmetry — if both (i,j) and (j,i) survive the mask, both entries appear in the result.

member.name: T:Graphs.Primitives.TriangleCount
member.summary: Pure graph operation: count 3-cycles (triangles) in an undirected via sorted-adjacency neighbor intersection. Lives in Graphs.Primitives rather than TDA.Primitives because the operation is structural (counts closed triplets in the adjacency relation) and has no topological content — TDA consumers depend on it, not the other way around.

remarks.para: Algorithm. Build sorted adjacency lists per node (CSR rows are not guaranteed sorted), then for each ordered edge u < v count shared neighbors w > v. The per-pair intersection is linear-merge over the two sorted lists. Each triangle {u, v, w} with u < v < w is counted exactly once.

Cost. O(Σ_v d(v)²) in the worst case, dominated by the intersection step on high-degree vertices. Fine for the proximity graphs SPC and diagnostics actually consume (~50–5000 nodes, bounded k). Not appropriate for dense general graphs; the Cycles diagnostic gates this behind a node-count cap.

member.name: M:Graphs.Primitives.UnionFind.WriteRootSizesTo(System.Span{System.Int32})
member.summary: Walks the parent array once and writes the size of each component (one entry per UF root) into . Returns the number of roots written. must have capacity at least N.
member.remarks: O(N), zero allocation. Sizes are written in the order roots are encountered while scanning indices 0..N-1; this ordering carries no semantic meaning — callers should treat the output as a multiset. Relies on _size[root] being maintained at union time, which is why this UF carries union-by-size in the first place.

member.name: T:Graphs.Distance.IDistanceMetric
member.summary: Struct-constrained distance metric. Implementations must be so the JIT devirtualises and inlines into hot loops (e.g. ImplicitPrims).

remarks.para: Properties. Every metric also declares a descriptor — its domain constraints, range, and the right bandwidth-estimation strategy. The descriptor is consulted once at graph-build time (input validation, bandwidth dispatch) and never touches the hot path. Implementations should return a cached/static instance from the getter — the JIT will fold the constant at the call site.

member.name: T:Graphs.Distance.BandwidthStrategy
member.summary: How bandwidth should be estimated for a given metric — consumed by the graph-construction layer's bandwidth dispatch (Pass 3). The enum lives here in Pass 2 so every metric struct can declare its preference up front; Pass 3 wires the dispatch in .

member.name: F:Graphs.Distance.BandwidthStrategy.MadConsistencyFactor
member.summary: MAD of nearest-neighbor distances rescaled by the kernel's MAD-to-σ consistency factor (the historical default). Correct for Euclidean / Manhattan / Minkowski distances in moderate dimensions where NN distances are approximately distributed as half-normal / exponential / Cauchy draws.

member.name: F:Graphs.Distance.BandwidthStrategy.QuantileNormalized
member.summary: Normalize NN distances to [0, 1] by dividing by a high quantile (e.g. 95th percentile), then apply the standard MAD dispatch in normalized space. Right for bounded metrics (JSD, FisherRao/Simplex, Cosine) where MAD-on-raw-distances is scale-mismatched against the consistency factors.

member.name: F:Graphs.Distance.BandwidthStrategy.LogScaleHyperbolic
member.summary: MAD computed on log(d + 1) of NN distances, then back-transformed. Right for hyperbolic metrics (Poincaré) where the NN distance distribution is roughly log-normal and raw MAD is dominated by boundary-region outliers.
